policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Word-order variant only; ASV 'they came unto the tomb' fixes English order regardless of whether the Greek puts the verb before or after the prepositional phrase.
ASV has only 'bringing the spices which they had prepared'; nothing renders the added 'and certain others with them' of r01.
ASV renders the verse-initial connective 'And', which serves either the postpositive δέ of the base or the καί of r01; the wording is otherwise identical.
ASV reads 'the body of the Lord Jesus' in the text and relegates the shorter reading to the margin ('Some ancient authorities omit of the Lord Jesus'), so the text follows the longer r01.
ASV 'while they were perplexed thereabout' renders the simplex and the διά-compound alike; the prefix has no English exponent.
ASV 'in dazzling apparel' uses a collective noun that does not show whether the Greek was singular ἐσθῆτι or plural ἐσθήσεσιν.
ASV 'bowed down their faces to the earth' is plural, matching τὰ πρόσωπα against the singular τὸ πρόσωπον of r01.

Both candidates carry the same words, differing only in SBLGNT bracketing and punctuation. ASV prints 'He is not here, but is risen' with the omission only in the margin, and no candidate omits the clause, so the English cannot separate them.
Word-order variant only (object before or after ὅτι δεῖ); English syntax forces 'that the Son of man must be delivered up' either way, and the base differs from r01 only in ellipsis notation.
The variant is the Greek article before the proper name, which ASV 'Mary Magdalene' leaves untranslated in either case.

ASV makes 'and the other women with them told these things unto the apostles' an independent clause with a finite main verb; the relative αἳ of r01 would require 'who told these things', which the ASV does not have.
ASV 'these words' renders the demonstrative ταῦτα; r01's αὐτῶν would give 'their words', and 'in their sight' already renders the separate ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν.
Both candidates contain the whole of verse 12, differing only in SBLGNT bracketing; ASV prints the verse with the omission noted in the margin, so no candidate is excluded.
ASV 'he seeth the linen cloths by themselves' has no rendering of the added participle κείμενα ('lying') in r01.
The candidates are accentual/orthographic forms of the same pronoun; ASV 'departed to his home' (margin 'wondering with himself') is compatible with each.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'two of them were going that very day' does not reveal the Greek position of the temporal phrase.
The variant adds only the Greek article before the name; ASV 'Jesus himself' leaves it untranslated either way.
ASV 'And they stood still, looking sad' renders the third-person aorist ἐστάθησαν; r01's ἐστε would give second-person 'and ye are sad' inside the question.

ASV 'And one of them, named Cleopas' could render the bare εἷς ὀνόματι with 'of them' supplied from context, the explicit εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν of r01, or the relative ᾧ ὄνομα of r02; the verse's only note is an alternative rendering, which cannot decide a reading.
ASV renders both Ναζαρηνός and Ναζωραῖος as 'the Nazarene', so the English form does not distinguish the two spellings.
The variant is a particle in the stacked ἀλλά γε (καὶ) σὺν πᾶσιν τούτοις; ASV 'Yea and besides all this' can render the cluster with or without καί.
ASV 'it is now the third day' has an adverb 'now' that may render σήμερον or be supplied idiomatically for ἄγει; the English neither requires nor excludes the added word.
ὀρθριναί and ὄρθριαι are alternative forms of the same adjective; ASV 'having been early at the tomb' fits either.
The variant is the verse-initial connective; ASV routinely opens a verse with 'And' whether or not καί stands in the Greek, so the English does not settle it.
Aorist against imperfect; ASV's simple past 'he interpreted' renders either.
ASV 'the things concerning himself' is the natural English for a pronoun referring back to the subject, whether the Greek is reflexive ἑαυτοῦ or plain αὐτοῦ.
Aorist against imperfect; ASV 'he made as though he would go further' does not mark the aspect.
πορρώτερον and πορρωτέρω are alternative comparative forms of the same adverb, both rendered 'further'.
ASV 'the day is now far spent' renders the adverb ἤδη, which r01 omits.
ASV 'Was not our heart burning within us' renders ἐν ἡμῖν, which r01 omits.
ASV joins the second clause without a conjunction — 'while he spake to us in the way, while he opened to us the scriptures' — where r01's καὶ ὡς would give 'and while he opened'.
The simplex and συν-compound participle are both rendered 'gathered together' in ASV.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'The Lord is risen indeed' fixes English order irrespective of where ὄντως stands in the Greek.
ASV 'he himself stood in the midst of them' has no rendering of the added subject ὁ Ἰησοῦς in r01.
ASV prints 'and saith unto them, Peace be unto you' in the text, with the omission only in the margin, so the text carries the longer r01.
ASV 'questionings arise in your heart' is singular, matching τῇ καρδίᾳ against the plural ταῖς καρδίαις of r01.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'that it is I myself' renders either arrangement of ἐγώ εἰμι αὐτός.
Both candidates contain all of verse 40 and differ only in SBLGNT bracketing; ASV prints the verse with the omission in the margin, so neither is excluded.
ἔδειξεν and the ἐπι-compound ἐπέδειξεν are both rendered 'showed'; the prefix has no English exponent here.
ASV text reads only 'a piece of a broiled fish' and puts the honeycomb in the margin ('Many ancient authorities add and a honeycomb'), so the text follows the shorter base reading.
πρὸς αὐτούς and the simple dative αὐτοῖς are both rendered 'unto them' after a verb of speaking.
ASV 'These are my words' renders the possessive μου, which r01 omits.
The variant adds only the Greek article before ψαλμοῖς; ASV 'and the psalms' supplies the English article either way.
ASV 'Thus it is written, that the Christ should suffer' has no second clause answering r01's added καὶ οὕτως ἔδει ('and thus it behooved').
ASV text reads 'repentance and remission of sins', rendering καί, and its note 'Some ancient authorities read unto' assigns εἰς (r01) to the margin.

Nominative plural against accusative singular participle; English 'beginning from Jerusalem' is uninflected, and the note bearing on the phrase is an alternative rendering, which cannot decide a reading.

ASV 'Ye are witnesses of these things' opens with no connective, which excludes r02's δέ; whether the copula stands in the Greek (base) or is supplied for a verbless clause (r01) the English is the same.
ASV renders both ἀποστέλλω and the ἐξ-compound as 'send forth', so the prefix is not visible in the English.
ASV 'tarry ye in the city' has no rendering of the added Ἱερουσαλήμ in r01.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'clothed with power from on high' places the modifier by English idiom, not by the Greek order.
ASV 'he led them out' already renders the compound verb ἐξήγαγεν, so it does not show whether a separate ἔξω stood in the Greek.
ASV 'until they were over against Bethany' renders ἕως πρός; r01's εἰς would give simple motion 'as far as to Bethany', without the 'over against'.
Both candidates contain the clause and differ only in SBLGNT bracketing; ASV prints 'and was carried up into heaven' with the omission in the margin, so neither is excluded.
Both candidates contain προσκυνήσαντες αὐτόν and differ only in bracketing; ASV prints 'they worshipped him, and' with the omission in the margin.
ASV has only 'blessing God'; r01's αἰνοῦντες καὶ would add 'praising and', which the ASV does not render.
ASV ends at 'blessing God' with no 'Amen', so the added Ἀμήν of r01 is unrendered.
